equity_bridge.item: Eneabba rare earths refinery equity, probability-weighted and floored at zero
equity_bridge.note: Side valuation, hand-built at the 9.5% WACC and 14x terminal cap, against claims of ~1,577 (Rare Earths net debt 876.9 at 30 June 2026 + ~700 to complete, taking the top of the 1.7-1.8bn estimate plus capitalised EFA interest). Bear (25%): commissioning slips, spot-level prices, EBITDA ~50 -> enterprise value far below the loan, equity 0 because the EFA loan is non-recourse. Base (50%): 16ktpa REO on stockpile feed, ~600 revenue and ~250 EBITDA from FY2030 -> EV ~1,700, equity ~125. Bull (25%): floor-style pricing and blended feed, ~900 revenue and ~450 EBITDA -> EV ~3,350, equity ~1,770. 0.25x0 + 0.5x125 + 0.25x1,770 = 505. Product mix and operating cost are NOT disclosed in the filings held here; the revenue and margin figures are the analyst's estimate and the single least certain number in this valuation.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle normalisation; no historical CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (+9.9%) diverges from revenue (+0.5%) by far more than 30%: the FY2020 base is depressed by the Deterra demerger and FY2025 equity is after 351 of impairments. EPS and owner FCF are negative in FY2025, so their CAGRs are undefined.
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 vs FY2022 and FY2020 annual rows. Revenue through FY2022 includes Sierra Rutile (demerged 2022). Share-based payments run at about 1% of revenue and were stable, so owner FCF and reported FCF trend together; both are negative from FY2023 on construction capex.

scenario_narratives.base: Mineral sands mean-reverts. FY2026 is a trough (H1 underlying EBITDA 41 against 218 a year earlier) caused by weak pigment demand, a customer administration and competitor zircon discounting, with Cataby and the SR2 kiln idled. Zircon volumes hold, synthetic rutile contracts are reset on minimum revenue terms, Balranald ramps, and revenue returns to about 1,170 by FY2030 at a 36% underlying margin, a little under the five-year average. Eneabba is commissioned in 2027 and on base assumptions is worth roughly what it cost.
scenario_narratives.bull: The titanium feedstock cycle turns as pigment inventories clear and Rio Tinto's RTIT review tightens merchant supply. Cataby and SR2 restart, Balranald runs at nameplate with rare earth credits, and zircon pricing recovers toward FY2022-23 levels, taking margins back to 43% underlying. The same weight also carries the Eneabba bull outcome (floor-style Western pricing, blended feed above stockpile rates), which sits in the bridge item rather than in these flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: The downturn is structural rather than cyclical: Chinese zircon supply keeps prices down, pigment customers consolidate or fail, the synthetic rutile kilns stay shut, and a stronger AUD compresses USD revenue against AUD costs. Revenue stays under 1,000 and margins settle near 25%, below even FY2025. Eneabba slips again or meets spot-level prices and its equity is worth nothing; the non-recourse EFA loan is what stops that loss reaching the mineral sands balance sheet.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical valued on mid-cycle mineral sands cash flow, with a government-funded, non-recourse growth project held apart as a floored option. The mineral sands flows alone do not cover the price; roughly a fifth of the weighted value is the Eneabba option and that rests on undisclosed refinery economics.
key_risks_to_valuation: Eneabba revenue and operating cost are analyst estimates: product mix, price terms in the offtake and unit costs are not in the filings held. The 505 bridge value moves by about 44 for every 100 change in the bull-case equity value.
The mid-cycle margin is a judgment: each point of terminal mineral sands margin is worth roughly 0.12 per share.
Rehabilitation is deducted at the after-tax book provision (526, 1.21 per share); the provision has been revised upward repeatedly for closed sites.
Remaining Eneabba capital is taken at about 700 from 30 June 2026 using a third-party-reported 1.237bn spent to September; an overrun beyond the 75 EFA overrun allowance falls on Iluka.
Wimmera and metallisation are excluded entirely, both the capital and the return.

inputs.share_count_basis: 431.195m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim report) plus ~4.8m unvested share rights (FY2025 diluted weighted count 433.97m vs basic 428.81m). Held flat: share-based payments are expensed in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_note: RECOURSE (mineral sands) balance sheet only: MOFA drawn 310.0 + lease liabilities 82.0 (21.8 current + 60.2 non-current) less mineral-sands cash 36.8 (reported mineral sands net debt 273.2). The non-recourse EFA loan (897.5 drawn, Rare Earths net debt 876.9) is NOT here: it is netted inside the Eneabba equity-bridge item. Group reported net debt is 1,150.1.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report share-based payments expense note (13.6; FY2024 15.3). No net-share-settlement tax line; rights are satisfied through the employee share trust.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD build: 10-year ACGB ~4.4% risk-free, ~5.5% Australian ERP, beta ~1.2 for a cyclical single-commodity-family miner gives cost of equity ~11%; recourse leverage is light so WACC 9.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality and Eneabba execution risk are carried in the scenario flows and in the floored Eneabba bridge value, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities of 82.0 sit in net debt, lease principal (~11/yr) is not deducted from the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest since the 2022 Sierra Rutile demerger.
inputs.notes: MODEL: sum of parts on the owner-FCF component engine. (1) Mineral sands, including all corporate costs, is valued by a 10-year MID-CYCLE owner-FCF DCF: the flows ramp from the FY2026 trough (H1 underlying mineral sands EBITDA of 41) to a normalised margin, not from the latest year. (2) The Eneabba rare earths refinery is pre-revenue and funded by a loan that is non-recourse to Iluka, so it is valued separately as an equity-bridge item floored at zero per scenario and probability-weighted; its revenue, capex and EFA debt are all excluded from the engine flows and from net_debt. (3) The 20% Deterra Royalties stake is in the bridge at market value and its equity-accounted profit (12.3 in H1 FY2026) is excluded from the EBITDA margin path (matching-asset rule). (4) Rehabilitation provisions are deducted after tax in the bridge; rehabilitation cash spend is not in underlying EBITDA, so it is charged once. CONSEQUENCE: the bear/base/bull values differ only on the mineral sands axis; each carries the same probability-weighted Eneabba value, so the scenario spread understates the true dispersion while the weighted IV is exact. base_revenue is an FY2026 ESTIMATE (H1 actual 455.9 plus Q3 mineral sands revenue ~219 and a similar Q4), because the valuation date is six weeks from year end and year 1 of the build is FY2027. H2 FY2026 cash flow between the 30 June balance sheet and the start of year 1 is not modelled; the inventory selldown under way makes that omission conservative. last_fcf (FY2025 reported FCF -919.6 less share-based payments) is dominated by Eneabba and Balranald construction and is not a base for anything. ebitda_margin_path is underlying mineral sands EBITDA with share-based payments added back, so that the engine's explicit SBC line charges it once. Wimmera, metallisation and Cataby/SR2 restart beyond the bull path are not valued. Buybacks are immaterial (0.5 in FY2025): the flat count is a modelling convention, funded in practice by trust share issues. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.rationale: No cyclical recovery: Chinese zircon discounting persists, synthetic rutile kilns stay idle, margins settle below the FY2025 trough-year level of 30% as higher-cost ore replaces Jacinth-Ambrosia.

base.rationale: Mineral sands only. Revenue recovers from ~910 to ~1,170 by FY2030 (FY2023-25 average 1,159) and is then flat in real terms. Underlying margin 36.3% after share-based payments, against 38% for FY2021-25 and 35% over FY2015-25, all after corporate costs. Capex 12.5% of revenue covers sustaining spend and periodic mine replacement (FY2014-23 average 11.6%). Year-1 cash tax is low on FY2025-26 losses.

bull.rationale: Pigment cycle turns, Cataby and SR2 restart, Balranald at nameplate: revenue ~1,365 by FY2030 and margins back at FY2021/FY2023 levels (41-45%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the core business is loss-making at the half, recourse debt funds a dividend framework its free cash flow has not covered, and the refinery has already slipped a year. Base 50%: a return to a margin slightly below the five- and ten-year averages is the ordinary outcome for a cyclical bought in a trough. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs a pigment recovery, two restarts and a Balranald ramp together. The same weights are applied to the Eneabba bridge value.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
